issues.legal_issue: A valid rent deposit with the rent authority does not satisfy a tenant’s separate obligation to deposit rent in court during a pending eviction proceeding, and does not prevent the tenant’s defence from being struck out for failing to do so.
material_facts: The landlord brought an eviction suit on grounds other than rent default.
The tenant had been depositing rent with the rent authority because the landlord would not accept it, and those deposits were valid.
After the suit was filed and summons served, the tenant continued depositing rent with the rent authority rather than depositing it in court.
The tenant did not make the required court deposit within the prescribed time, and the landlord sought to have the tenant’s defence struck out.
issues.conclusion: The court upheld the order striking out the tenant’s defence. Once the eviction proceeding was instituted and the prescribed period after service of summons had expired, the tenant had to comply with the court-deposit procedure; valid deposits with the rent authority were no answer to the application to strike out the defence.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 17(1) and 17(3) of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1956, a tenant in a covered eviction suit must make the specified deposits in court, and failure permits the court to strike out the defence against delivery of possession. Sections 21 and 22, including section 22(3), govern deposits with the Controller in a different setting and do not displace section 17’s special, complete scheme once its requirements apply. The court approved the majority view in Siddheswar Paul v. Prakash Chandra Dutta, AIR 1964 Cal 105. It also observed that a valid deposit under section 21 prevents a rent-default eviction claim under section 13(1)(i), but does not excuse noncompliance with section 17 in an eviction proceeding on other grounds.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding and rent_deposited_with_rent_authority and summons_period_elapsed and rent_not_deposited_in_court

predicates.eviction_proceeding: A landlord has brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant.
predicates.rent_deposited_with_rent_authority: The tenant has deposited rent with the rent authority rather than paying it to the landlord.
predicates.summons_period_elapsed: The prescribed period after the tenant was served with notice of the eviction proceeding has expired.
predicates.rent_not_deposited_in_court: The tenant has failed to make the required rent deposit in the court hearing the eviction proceeding.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding is pending, the post-service period has expired, and the tenant deposited rent with the rent authority but failed to deposit it in court, the tenant’s defence is struck out for that noncompliance.
